A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProbeLLM study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H support reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing experiments across five benchmarks and 12 target models, baseline comparisons, mitigation experiments, and human evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Table 1, the mitigation results in Figure 9, and the appendix human evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same hierarchical MCTS, macro/micro generation, tool-based verification, failure-aware embeddings, clustering, and boundary-aware induction. Algorithm relocation does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU, SuperGLUE, MBPP, HellaSwag, and TruthfulQA and retain the same mitigation, model-generation, and human-evaluation scenarios. No evaluated task or domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: AutoDetect and PAIR retain the same participation in error-rate, clustering-quality, and human-quality comparisons. The error-rate comparison moves from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 3; the clustering comparison moves from Table 3 to Table 4.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings are retained, including 100 simulations per benchmark and 500 per target model in Appendix C.1, the baseline procedures in Appendix D, and GRPO with eight rollouts and two epochs in Appendix C.6.

E4.justification: Search-depth and tool-use analyses, alternative generators, macro/micro allocation, mitigation, model evolution, clustering sensitivity, and Appendix H case studies are all retained. Relocated plots do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain identical-seed initialization, 200 independent trials for each baseline, human-evaluation means and standard deviations, and the same uncertainty displays. The search-depth plot still reports standard deviations across 12 target models.

E6.justification: Matched main-text and appendix tables, plots, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Llama-3.1-8b error rates of 86% on MMLU and 90% on MBPP. Renumbering adds no results.

T1.justification: The failure definitions, utility objective, MCTS equations, clustering-consistency definition, and Appendix E assumptions, convergence proofs, and complexity analysis are retained. Mathematical differences are typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about benchmark-agnostic, budget-aware probing and verifiable discovery of structured failure modes.

C2.justification: Interpretations of search saturation, mitigation behavior, clustering stability, and evolving model weaknesses are unchanged. Appendix B.2 retains the qualification about verifiable answers and future open-ended evaluation; Appendix D retains the baseline-comparability caveat.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, experimental details, human-evaluation instructions, and Appendix G tool-integration code are retained. Section 4 still defers detailed prompts and configurations to the same linked toolkit and documentation.

R1.justification: The same 95 cited works and Appendix A research positioning are retained. Expanded bibliographic author names, citation formatting, and year-letter relabeling do not change the referenced work or contribution positioning.

P1.justification: v2 updates front matter to state ICML 2026 acceptance, condenses the AI-use disclosure, removes the B.4 subsection heading, and adjusts interface-location wording. Almost all substantive prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column layout with new typography, headers, a shaded abstract, and extensive display reflow. Figures 4–6 are renumbered, Tables 3–4 exchange numbers, and Algorithm 1 moves from Appendix B.4 to between C.8 and C.9. The underlying displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The extensive redesign and limited editorial changes preserve the same scientific argument, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information. Both versions remain readable; the new styling also disperses some supporting displays, notably Algorithm 1. These presentation tradeoffs do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
